children: Star Gold Corp. reported a net loss for the first quarter of fiscal 2027, with no operating revenue in the quarter as the company advanced permitting and technical fieldwork for its Longstreet project.
Net income: $(991,838) for Q1 2027 (three months ended July 31, 2026), compared with $(130,384) in the year‑ago quarter — an increase in loss of $861,454 year over year.
Diluted EPS: $(0.01) for Q1 2027; prior-year quarter: $0.00.
Revenue: No operating revenue reported for the three months ended July 31, 2026 or July 31, 2025.
Permitting milestones: Secured BLM and U.S. Forest Service approvals in May–June 2026 to begin hydrology, geology and geotechnical work at Longstreet.

Operational ramp-up: Resumed active fieldwork, including drilling, hydrology and technical studies to support an Environmental Impact Statement/Environmental Assessment and progress Longstreet toward production.
Exploration focus: Targeting multiple Longstreet prospects (North, Red Knob, Cyprus Ridge) with planned core and hydrology drilling programs.
Project funding plans: Management intends to pursue capital through equity, joint ventures and farm-outs to finance permitting, EIS/EA preparation and pre-production activities.
Organizational scaling: Increased technical, legal and consulting support, added D&O insurance and stepped up marketing to support permitting and investor engagement.
